title: Layered Material Blending System
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive layered material blending system on a 3D sphere. The system supports up to 4 material layers that can be added, removed, reordered, and blended with precise weight control.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e).
- PerspectiveCamera at (0, 0, 4), looking at origin.
- One main sphere (radius 1.2, 64x64 segments) at the origin using a ShaderMaterial.
- AmbientLight (intensity 0.3) and one DirectionalLight at (3, 5, 4) with intensity 1.0.
- OrbitControls for camera rotation.

## Material Layer System
Each layer has:
- `type`: one of 'diffuse', 'metallic', 'emissive', 'glass'
- `color`: a hex color value
- `weight`: float 0.0 to 1.0 (default 0.5)
- `blendMode`: one of 'normal', 'multiply', 'additive', 'screen'
- `roughness`: float 0.0 to 1.0
- `enabled`: boolean

Default initial state: Layer 0 is 'diffuse' with color 0x4488cc, weight 1.0, blendMode 'normal', roughness 0.5, enabled true. No other layers.

The ShaderMaterial must combine all enabled layers according to their weights and blend modes. Weights of all enabled layers must be normalized so they sum to exactly 1.0 before blending. The final material properties (color RGB, roughness, metalness, emissive contribution) are computed from the weighted blend.

## Layer Type Properties
- diffuse: metalness=0.0, base color contribution, no emissive
- metallic: metalness=1.0, reflective tint from color, no emissive
- emissive: metalness=0.0, adds emissive glow equal to color*weight
- glass: metalness=0.0, roughness forced to 0.05, transparency-like effect (alpha 0.3 base)

## HUD / UI Panel
Create a DOM panel (id='material-panel') on the left side, 280px wide, semi-transparent dark background.
- Display each layer as a row with: layer index, type label, a color swatch, weight slider (0-100 mapped to 0.0-1.0), blend mode dropdown, roughness slider, enable/disable checkbox, remove button (×).
- 'Add Layer' button (id='btn-add-layer') at the bottom. When clicked, adds a new layer of type 'metallic', color 0xffaa33, weight 0.5, blendMode 'normal', roughness 0.3, enabled true. Max 4 layers.
- 'Reset All' button (id='btn-reset') restores to the single default diffuse layer.
- Each layer row has class 'layer-row' and data-layer-index attribute.
- Weight sliders have class 'weight-slider'.
- Roughness sliders have class 'roughness-slider'.
- Blend mode dropdowns have class 'blend-select'.
- Enable checkboxes have class 'layer-toggle'.
- Remove buttons have class 'btn-remove'.

## Keyboard Controls
- Press '1','2','3','4' to toggle enable/disable of layer at that index (0-based: '1'=index 0, etc.).
- Press 'U' to undo the last state change (support at least 10 undo steps).
- Press 'R' to redo after undo.
- Press 'N' to cycle the blend mode of the currently selected layer (click a layer row to select it; selected row gets a highlight border). Cycle order: normal -> multiply -> additive -> screen -> normal.
- Press 'ArrowUp' / 'ArrowDown' to move the selected layer up/down in the stack order.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- `layers`: array of layer objects [{type, color, weight, blendMode, roughness, enabled}, ...]
- `layerCount`: number of layers
- `enabledCount`: number of enabled layers
- `normalizedWeights`: array of floats (normalized weights of enabled layers, 0 for disabled)
- `weightSum`: sum of normalizedWeights (must always === 1.0 when enabledCount > 0, 0 when none enabled)
- `finalColor`: {r, g, b} floats 0-1 of the blended result color
- `finalRoughness`: float, blended roughness
- `finalMetalness`: float, blended metalness
- `finalEmissive`: {r, g, b} floats 0-1
- `selectedLayerIndex`: integer or -1 if none selected
- `undoStackSize`: number of items in undo stack
- `redoStackSize`: number of items in redo stack
- `blendHistory`: array of last 5 blend computations as [{finalColor, finalRoughness, timestamp}]
- `sphereVisible`: boolean
- `frameCount`: integer incremented each animation frame

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame. Ensure all numerical values are NaN-free. The normalized weight invariant (sum === 1.0 for enabled layers) must hold at all times.
physics_constraints: Weight normalization conservation: sum of normalized weights of enabled layers must equal exactly 1.0 at all times when at least one layer is enabled. Blend computations must be NaN-free and all color channels clamped to [0,1]. Roughness and metalness must remain in [0,1]. Undo/redo must perfectly restore prior states including all layer properties.
